title_en: Wei Shuying, Qi Shuai v. Xinmin Municipal People's Government, Liaoning Province — dispute over forced removal of above-ground objects and administrative compensation
ruling_gist_en: For an appraisal institution that provides false evidentiary materials during litigation and obstructs the court's trial of a case, the people's court shall, in accordance with Article 59 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, impose penalties on the appraisal institution and its principal responsible persons and directly responsible persons.

full_text_en:
Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai v. Xinmin Municipal People’s Government, Liaoning Province — dispute over compulsory removal of above-ground objects and administrative compensation

Ruling Summary

People’s courts shall, in accordance with Article 59 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, impose penalties on appraisal institutions and their principal responsible persons and directly responsible persons for providing false evidentiary materials during litigation and obstructing the court’s trial.

Supreme People’s Court Administrative Ruling

(2015) Xing Jian Zi No. 1921

Re-applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Xinmin Municipal People’s Government, Liaoning Province. Domicile: No. 2, Nanjiao Road, Xinmin City.

Legal Representative: Xing Peng, Mayor.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Hao, Director of Xinmin Transportation Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Chi Hongying, Lawyer at Liaoning Shensheng Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Wei Shuying, female, Han nationality, residing at Xinliu Street, Xinmin City.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Qi Shuai, male, Han nationality, residing at Xinliu Street, Xinmin City.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Zhiqiang, Lawyer at Liaoning Bisheng Law Firm.

Re-applicant Xinmin Municipal People’s Government (hereinafter referred to as Xinmin Government), dissatisfied with the administrative judgment No. (2015) Liao Xing Zhong Zi No. 81 rendered by the Liaoning High People’s Court on April 24, 2015, in the case of Respondents Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai v. it concerning compulsory removal of above-ground objects and administrative compensation, filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court accepted the case on November 5, 2015, formed a collegial panel in accordance with law for review, and on the afternoon of December 16, 2015, organized a hearing in the Third Courtroom of the Second Circuit Court (Shenyang) of this Court, with the participation of agents ad litem Zhang Hao and Chi Hongying of the Re-applicant Xinmin Government, Respondents Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai and their agent ad litem Zhang Zhiqiang; Zhou Shijie, an appraisal technician from Shenyang Jiasen Forest Resources Asset Price Appraisal Firm (hereinafter referred to as Jiasen Appraisal Firm), appeared as a witness to be examined. The case has now been concluded upon review.

Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai had 7.2 mu (approximately 0.48 hectares) of contracted land on the east side of Qianyingzi Village, Xinmin City. Prior to 2008, they had been engaged in the cultivation and sale of nursery seedlings and ornamental trees on the contracted land. The Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway Passenger Dedicated Line passes through seven townships, towns, and subdistricts in Xinmin City, with a length of 55.655 kilometers within Xinmin City. The contracted land of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai fell within the scope of land used for this project. To facilitate the construction of the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway Passenger Dedicated Line project, on June 25, 2009, and December 18, 2013, Xinmin Government issued two announcements prohibiting rush planting and rush construction within the project land area. On December 21, 2013, Xinmin Government issued the “Implementation Plan for Land Acquisition and Relocation Compensation for the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway Passenger Dedicated Line (Xinmin Section) Project,” in which the compensation standard for Prunus cerasifera (purple-leaf plum) was set at RMB 50 per plant in the appendix. On March 9, 2014, Xinmin Government organized personnel to inspect the seedlings on the contracted land of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai, confirming that 23,116 three-year-old purple-leaf plum trees were planted on the contracted land. Three persons from Jiasen Appraisal Firm, Cong Rijian, Pei Haifeng, and Zhang Jiqiang, participated in the inspection. On March 9, 2014, Xinmin Government issued the “Notice on Clearing Illegally Rush-planted and Rush-constructed Above-ground Objects and Facilities along the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway,” requiring the parties involved in rush planting and rush construction to voluntarily clear the above-ground objects and facilities within three days from the date of issuance; if not cleared voluntarily within the time limit, the public security organs and relevant law enforcement departments would carry out compulsory clearing in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. On March 13, 2014, Xinmin Government carried out compulsory removal of the purple-leaf plum trees on the 7.2 mu contracted land of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai. Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai, dissatisfied, filed a lawsuit with the Shenyang Intermediate People’s Court, requesting a declaration that the compulsory removal was illegal and compensation for economic losses of RMB 1.47 million. It is further found that on October 17, 2014, the Ministry of Land and Resources issued Letter No. Guotu Zi Han [2014] 528, the “Reply on the Construction Land for the New Beijing-Shenyang Railway Passenger Dedicated Line (Shenyang, Fuxin, Chaoyang Sections),” approving the conversion of a total of 1,101.3334 hectares of collectively owned agricultural land, including the contracted land in question, into construction land and the handling of land acquisition procedures. On November 7, 2014, the Liaoning Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued Letter No. Liao Guotu Zi Han [2014] 218, “Letter Forwarding the Reply of the Ministry of Land and Resources on the Construction Land for the New Beijing-Shenyang Railway Passenger Dedicated Line (Shenyang, Fuxin, Chaoyang Sections).” It is also found that after the second-instance judgment became effective, Xinmin Government commissioned Jiasen Appraisal Firm to conduct a price appraisal of the purple-leaf plum trees of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai. On August 28, 2015, Jiasen Appraisal Firm issued the “Appraisal Report on Asset Value of Purple-Leaf Plum Trees Owned by Qi Shuai Involved in the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway Project” (Shen Jia Lin Ping Zi [2015] No. 530; hereinafter “Appraisal Report No. 530”), determining that the price of the purple-leaf plum seedlings of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai was RMB 5 per plant. The appraisal technicians were Zhou Shijie and Zhang Jiliang. Xinmin Government submitted this appraisal report to this Court as new evidence, requesting the reversal of the first- and second-instance judgments.

The first-instance judgment held that: Article 25, paragraph 2 of the “Liaoning Province Implementation Measures of the Land Administration Law of the PRC” stipulates: “Trees, seedlings, and buildings or structures that are rush-planted or rush-constructed after the date of the land acquisition announcement shall not be compensated.” The evidence submitted by Xinmin Government could not prove that the land used by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai had been approved for acquisition by the competent authority and that a land acquisition announcement had been issued at the time of the compulsory removal. Meanwhile, according to the evidence provided by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai, it could be proven that Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai had been engaged in the business of cultivating and selling seedlings prior to 2008, and before the land acquisition and relocation for the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway, they did not change the types of seedlings originally planted and did not engage in rush planting. Xinmin Government’s compulsory removal based on the ground that Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai had rush-planted after June 2009 lacked factual basis and should be declared illegal. Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai have the right to obtain administrative compensation for the property losses caused by the illegal compulsory removal. Since the purple-leaf plum trees of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai had been compulsorily removed and were lost, making appraisal impossible, compensation could be made by reference to the standard specified in the land acquisition compensation plan involved. Therefore, Xinmin Government should compensate for the loss of purple-leaf plum seedlings: 23,116 plants x RMB 50/plant = RMB 1,155,800. In accordance with Article 57, paragraph 2, subparagraph (2) of the “Supreme People’s Court’s Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC” and Article 4, subparagraph (2) of the “State Compensation Law of the PRC,” the court ruled: (1) declare the compulsory removal act of Xinmin Government illegal; (2) Xinmin Government shall pay compensation for the loss of above-ground plants to Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai in the amount of RMB 1,155,800 within fifteen days from the date the judgment becomes effective. Xinmin Government appealed.

The second-instance judgment held that: Xinmin Government, without having obtained the land acquisition approval or issued a land acquisition announcement, directly determined that the purple-leaf plum seedlings planted by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai were rush-planted trees, which obviously violated the provisions of the Liaoning Province Implementation Measures of the Land Administration Law of the PRC. Although Xinmin Government submitted in the second instance evidence that the land in question had been approved for acquisition, that evidence could not prove the legality of the compulsory removal of above-ground seedlings. Xinmin Government argued that the purple-leaf plum seedlings planted by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai should be determined as rush-planted under Article 3, subparagraph (9) of the “Guiding Opinions on Improving the Land Acquisition Compensation and Resettlement System” (Ministry of Land and Resources, Guo Tu Zi Fa [2004] No. 238). However, since Xinmin Government did not notify Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai in writing of the land acquisition situation before lawfully submitting the land acquisition for approval, determining the act of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai as rush planting under this provision still lacked factual basis. In accordance with Article 61, subparagraph (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC before amendment, the court ruled to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Xinmin Government applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. Xinmin Government’s confirmation that there were 23,116 purple-leaf plum trees on the contracted land of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai was merely a record of objective fact and could not demonstrate the reasonableness of plant density. 2. The compensation standard of RMB 50 per plant in the compensation plan was for mature trees of the same kind and not applicable to the seedlings planted by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai. 3. Xinmin Government commissioned Jiasen Appraisal Firm to appraise the seedlings of Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai, and the conclusion was that the price of the planted seedlings was RMB 5 per plant. Applying for retrial under Article 91, subparagraphs (2) and (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, requesting reversal of the first- and second-instance judgments and change of judgment to compensate Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai in the amount of RMB 115,580.

Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai responded: 1. The evidence for the compensation amounts in the first- and second-instance judgments all came from Xinmin Government, which was objective and fair, and should be upheld. 2. As land requisitionees for the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway (Xinmin Section), Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai should enjoy equal treatment with other requisitionees. 3. On September 9, 2015, Xinmin Government voluntarily reached an agreement with Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai, agreeing to compensate according to the effective judgment, but now it has applied for retrial, reneging on its promise and acting in bad faith.

Upon review, this Court holds that: Xinmin Government, without having obtained the land acquisition approval or issued a land acquisition announcement, determined that the purple-leaf plum trees planted by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai were rush-planted and carried out compulsory removal, lacking factual and legal basis. The first- and second-instance judgments declaring the act illegal are not disputed by either party, and this Court also confirms that. Xinmin Government’s illegal compulsory removal caused property losses to Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai and shall compensate in accordance with law.

I. Regarding the number of purple-leaf plum trees

Article 53 of the “Supreme People’s Court’s Several Provisions on Evidence in Administrative Litigation” provides: “People’s courts shall base their judgments in administrative cases on the facts of the case proven by evidence.” On September 16, 2014, Jiasen Appraisal Firm issued the “Explanation on the Investigation of the Assets of Purple-Leaf Plum Trees Owned by Qi Shuai” (hereinafter “Explanation on Purple-Leaf Plum Trees”), stating that: Jiasen Appraisal Firm, commissioned by the Xinmin Municipal Land and Housing Acquisition Office, conducted an investigation on March 9, 2014, jointly with personnel from Xinliu Subdistrict and Qianyingzi Village Committee, determining that the purple-leaf plum trees owned by Qi Shuai were three years old, with a total number of 23,116 plants. This investigation result was a document formed during the seedling verification process. Xinmin Government also acknowledged it and submitted it as its own evidence to the first-instance court. During the trial and cross-examination in the first instance, neither party raised any objection to the authenticity or legality of this evidence. The first instance admitted this evidence and determined the number of purple-leaf plum trees compulsorily removed from Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai, which was not improper. Xinmin Government’s retrial application claims that the “Explanation on Purple-Leaf Plum Trees” could not demonstrate the reasonableness of plant density, thus negating the probative force of the evidence. However, it did not provide sufficient counterevidence to overturn it, and during this Court’s hearing, the agent ad litem of Xinmin Government stated that it would no longer raise objections regarding the number of purple-leaf plum trees. Therefore, this Court does not support Xinmin Government’s ground for retrial concerning the number of purple-leaf plum trees.

II. Regarding the compensation standard

Article 36, subparagraph (8) of the State Compensation Law of the PRC provides that where damage is caused to the property rights of citizens, legal persons, or other organizations, compensation shall be paid in accordance with direct losses. Direct losses mean the market value of the damaged property. The illegal compulsory removal of purple-leaf plum trees planted by Wei Shuying and Qi Shuai by Xinmin Government should be compensated according to the market appraisal price of the purple-leaf plum trees. In the situation where the trees had been compulsorily removed and could not be appraised based on their present condition, the first- and second-instance judgments, by adopting the standard of RMB 50 per plant as stipulated in Xinmin Government’s acquisition compensation plan for compensation, reflected the basic principle of market price compensation, and the judgment result was not improper. Xinmin Government contends that the compensation standard of RMB 50 per plant in the compensation plan was for mature purple-leaf plum trees. However, such a conclusion cannot be drawn from the wording of the compensation plan, and Xinmin Government has not provided any other relevant evidence to prove its claim. Xinmin Government submitted Appraisal Report No. 530 as “new evidence” to this Court. According to Article 52 of the Supreme People’s Court’s Several Provisions on Evidence in Administrative Litigation, “new evidence” for retrial refers to: (1) evidence that should have been permitted to be submitted after an extension in the first-instance proceedings but was not permitted; (2) evidence that a party applied to obtain in the first-instance proceedings in accordance with law but was not permitted or obtained, and which the people’s court obtained in the second-instance proceedings; (3) evidence discovered after the expiration of the time limit for adducing evidence and submitted by the plaintiff or a third party. In this case, Xinmin Government did not apply for an appraisal of the price of the purple-leaf plum trees in the first- or second-instance proceedings. The appraisal conclusion obtained by commissioning an appraisal institution after the second-instance judgment became effective is manifestly not “new evidence” that should be admitted for retrial.

III. Regarding the authenticity of the appraisal report

Jiasen Appraisal Firm, commissioned by Xinmin Government, produced Appraisal Report No. 530, which seriously violates appraisal procedures; the appraisal conclusion lacks factual basis and is not authentic; it cannot serve as a basis for determining the compensation price for the purple-leaf plum trees in question. The main reasons are as follows:

(1) According to Article 11 of the “Asset Appraisal Standards — Appraisal Procedures,” a registered asset appraiser shall first clarify the appraisal purpose. The appraisal purpose determined in Appraisal Report No. 530 was: “to verify the total asset value of purple-leaf plum trees owned by Qi Shuai, objectively and fairly determine the compensation standard for the acquisition of purple-leaf plum trees, and provide a basis for the commissioning party’s acquisition compensation.” This appraisal purpose conflicts with the objective facts. First, the Liaoning High People’s Court had already rendered a second-instance judgment on April 24, 2015, confirming that Xinmin Government’s compulsory removal of purple-leaf plum trees was illegal, requiring compensation (赔偿) rather than compensation (补偿). Second, Xinmin Government had already formulated in 2013 the land acquisition and relocation compensation implementation plan for the Beijing-Shenyang High-Speed Railway project (Xinmin Section), specifying compensation standards for various above-ground objects including purple-leaf plum trees. Therefore, the appraisal purpose determined in Appraisal Report No. 530 cannot be established.

(2) According to Article 6 of the “Asset Appraisal Standards — Appraisal Procedures,” on-site investigation is a basic appraisal procedure, and a registered asset appraiser shall not arbitrarily omit basic appraisal procedures. Jiasen Appraisal Firm claimed that the on-site investigation of the purple-leaf plum trees in question was the investigation carried out by the firm on March 9, 2014. First, the investigation conducted on March 9, 2014, occurred before Jiasen Appraisal Firm accepted this asset appraisal commission, and the 2014 investigation was not conducted for the purpose of asset value appraisal. Xinmin Government stated in both the second instance and the retrial application that the 2014 investigation was merely procedural data for household-by-household survey, and this investigation could not replace the investigation procedure in this appraisal. Second, the personnel participating in the investigation on March 9, 2014, were Cong Rijian, Pei Haifeng, and Zhang Jiqiang from Jiasen Appraisal Firm, which were completely different from the personnel who completed this appraisal. Third, the investigation form of March 9, 2014, contained only descriptions of “tree age 3 years, tree height 1.2 meters” for the purple-leaf plum trees, lacking specific statements and records of ground diameter, diameter at breast height, crown width, number of branches, and other conditions. Fourth, the image data from the investigation of March 9, 2014, consisted of only a few on-site photos, without information such as shooting location, shooting time, and scale, making it impossible to accurately reproduce the full appearance of the purple-leaf plum trees in question. Therefore, Appraisal Report No. 530 lacked an on-site investigation procedure.

(3) The appraisal base date determined in Appraisal Report No. 530 was August 28, 2015, which is not the date when the purple-leaf plum trees in question were compulsorily removed. During this Court’s hearing, Jiasen Appraisal Firm stated that the market price of nursery seedlings had been declining year by year since 2013. Using August 2015 as the appraisal base date makes it difficult to accurately reflect the value of the purple-leaf plum trees in question at the time of compulsory removal.

(4) According to Article 19 of the “Asset Appraisal Standards — Appraisal Procedures,” a registered asset appraiser shall conduct investigations through various methods to obtain the basic data required for the appraisal business, understand the current condition of the appraisal object, and pay attention to the legal ownership of the appraisal object. The purple-leaf plum trees in question were three years old and had undergone one stubble cutting in the spring of 2012. Jiasen Appraisal Firm stated that it used one-year-old seedlings as the subject of price inquiry during the appraisal, rather than using the entire three-year-old tree as the subject of price inquiry, making the subject of inquiry seriously inaccurate.

(5) The appraisal method used in Appraisal Report No. 530 was the market price method. According to Articles 22 to 24 of the “Asset Appraisal Standards — Appraisal Procedures,” a registered asset appraiser shall collect appraisal materials according to business needs, and conduct necessary analysis, summarization, and organization to form a basis for assessment and estimation. The appraisal materials shall include inquiry records, price inquiry results, industry information, analysis data, and other forms. Jiasen Appraisal Firm stated during the hearing that the appraisal technicians conducted market price inquiries, but could not provide accurate information on the subjects of inquiry, methods of inquiry, process of inquiry, or how the appraisers formed the preliminary appraisal conclusion and final appraisal conclusion through specific analysis, calculation, and judgment. The appraisal conclusion lacks any factual basis.

(6) According to the provisions of the “Asset Appraisal Standards — Working Papers,” a registered asset appraiser shall prepare and manage working papers when performing asset appraisal business. Working papers include management working papers and operational working papers, wherein operational working papers shall include market survey and data analysis materials, relevant historical and forecast data, price inquiry records, other expert appraisals and professional reports, etc. Jiasen Appraisal Firm claimed to have conducted online and telephone price inquiries, consulted industry experts, and performed other work. However, it admitted during the hearing that it did not prepare or preserve any working papers, and thus could not prove that it had conducted the relevant price inquiries, expert consultations, and other work.

(7) According to Article 6 of the “Asset Appraisal Standards — Appraisal Reports,” an appraisal report shall provide necessary information to enable users of the appraisal report to reasonably understand the appraisal conclusion. The conclusion of Appraisal Report No. 530 was that the current market price of the purple-leaf plum trees in question was RMB 5 per plant. However, in the land acquisition and relocation compensation implementation plan formulated by Xinmin Government in 2013, the compensation price for purple-leaf plum trees was RMB 50 per plant, a tenfold difference. Yet the appraisal report provided no explanation or analysis of this difference.

The Appraisal Report No. 530 produced by Jiasen Appraisal Firm violates appraisal procedures, and its appraisal conclusion lacks basic factual basis. It constitutes an act of providing false evidentiary materials and obstructing the trial of the case by the people’s court. Pursuant to Article 59, paragraph 1, subparagraph (2) and paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, Jiasen Appraisal Firm and its principal responsible persons and directly responsible persons shall be subject to a fine sanction.

In summary, Xinmin Government’s application for retrial does not meet the circumstances specified in Article 91, subparagraphs (2) and (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. In accordance with Article 74 of the Supreme People’s Court’s Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Xinmin Municipal People’s Government is rejected.

Presiding Judge: Guo Xiujiang

Judge: Dong Hua

Judge: Fan Xiangyang

December 23, 2015
